analysis.investment_thesis: Jayaswal Neco is a cyclical, capital-heavy steel business carrying D/E of 0.91 and generating a negative ROE of -0.87% — failing every core criterion I demand before investing a single rupee. With ₹554 Cr annual finance costs devouring profits and net income collapsing from ₹2,247 Cr (2022, likely one-time) to just ₹113 Cr (2025), there is no reliable earnings power to anchor a long-term holding.
key_strengths: Free cash flow turned strongly positive in 2025 (₹1,144 Cr OCF), funding meaningful debt repayment
Total debt declining steadily: ₹3,845 Cr (2022) → ₹2,753 Cr (2025), showing some discipline
Promoter holding at 55.15% meets the minimum threshold, suggesting alignment
key_risks: D/E of 0.91 is triple my maximum threshold of 0.3 — balance sheet risk is unacceptable
Net profit crashing: ₹2,247 Cr (2022) → ₹227 Cr (2023) → ₹113 Cr (2025), exposing 2022 as a one-time windfall
Finance costs of ₹554 Cr in 2025 exceed net profit by 4.9x — the debt is strangling the business
red_flags: ROE of -0.87% and ROCE of 2.93% — destroying shareholder value, not creating it
Historic reckless debt-funded expansion: borrowings grew from ₹1,244 Cr (2011) to ₹4,114 Cr (2016), CWIP ballooned to ₹3,163 Cr — classic capital misallocation
Revenue completely stagnant: ₹5,955 Cr (2022) to ₹5,985 Cr (2025) — zero real growth over three years
P/E of 25x on collapsing and unreliable earnings — valuation makes no sense for this quality level
Steel sector is inherently cyclical and commodity-driven — the complete opposite of the predictable consumer businesses I seek
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Jayaswal Neco fails my fundamental screen at every checkpoint. The D/E of 0.91 alone is disqualifying — I built DMart with essentially zero debt because leverage amplifies mistakes and destroys businesses in downturns. Here, ₹554 Cr in annual finance costs is consuming what little operating profit the business generates (EBITDA ₹947 Cr), leaving almost nothing for shareholders after servicing lenders. The negative ROE of -0.87% tells me plainly: this business is destroying capital, not compounding it. The 2022 net profit of ₹2,247 Cr is a statistical mirage — almost certainly debt restructuring gains or one-time items — as the very next year collapsed to ₹227 Cr. I never invest in a story; I invest in verifiable, repeated earnings, and there are none here.

The business history confirms a pattern I actively avoid: management that funded aggressive expansion with borrowed money (CWIP of ₹3,163 Cr by 2015, debt of ₹4,114 Cr by 2016), ran into financial distress, and is now slowly deleveraging. The OCF of ₹1,388 Cr in 2025 is encouraging but is almost entirely consumed repaying past mistakes (Financing CF -₹1,086 Cr). Steel is a commodity sector with no pricing power, no moat, and no predictable demand — everything I avoid in favour of branded consumer businesses. At P/E of 25x on earnings that are evaporating, the market is pricing in a recovery that the fundamentals do not support. I would not own this at any price in the current condition.
